central_topic: Selecting a small subset of benchmark items using source models' per-item binary results to predict a new LLM's full-benchmark score and ranking, via an IRT-style logistic latent model with Fisher-information D-optimal item selection and a model-assisted difference estimator, with emphasis on new models stronger than all source models.
core_methods: Model-assisted difference estimator (model prediction plus observed-sample residual)
Fisher-information / D-optimal item selection in a latent ability space
Multidimensional IRT-style logistic latent model with MAP ability estimation
result_driven_themes: Prediction error and rank correlation degrade for target models whose ability lies above the source range

queries.query: predicting benchmark performance of new stronger language models extrapolation beyond source model range
queries.rationale: Targets gap intro-strong-target-motivation: the introduction calls the better-than-all-sources case the hardest and most practically relevant but cites no prior evidence that benchmark or ability prediction degrades out of range or that frontier-model evaluation is where savings matter.

queries.query: multidimensional item response theory Fisher information item selection computerized adaptive testing
queries.rationale: Targets gap related-work-irt-fisher-design: the 'Estimation and design tools' paragraph rests the logistic latent model and Fisher-information item selection on one NLP-leaderboard IRT paper and Kiefer; foundational multidimensional IRT, MAP ability and CAT item-selection sources are missing.

queries.query: model-assisted survey sampling difference estimator regression estimator
queries.rationale: Targets gap related-work-model-assisted-estimator: the estimator adding the mean residual of revealed items to a model-based prediction is the classical survey-sampling difference/generalized regression estimator, currently linked only to prediction-powered inference.

queries.query: PPI++ efficient prediction-powered inference active statistical inference labeled sample model predictions
queries.rationale: Same related-work-model-assisted-estimator paragraph: one or two bridging citations connecting the survey-sampling estimator to its modern ML descendants beyond the original prediction-powered inference paper already in the bibliography.

forbidden_query_patterns: generic 'efficient LLM evaluation' or 'benchmarking' phrasing without a named method
re-searching benchmark-subset comparators already cited (anchor points, tinyBenchmarks, metabench, PromptEval, ONEBench)
re-searching dataset/benchmark sources, stacked generalization or the Kiefer equivalence theorem
internal metric names such as combined_score or strong_targets
